newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds were higher at the close of a quiet trading session, with the Swiss franc above Tuesday's lows.
The franc weighed on prices on Tuesday when it hit its lowest level versus the dollar since early February 1995, as the dollar rose to 1.2964 francs.

The franc's weakness has tended to push Swiss domestic rates higher, especially in the short end, although the impact has lessened of late, traders said. Short-term interest rates reflected by the LIFFE's three-month EuroSwiss contract have also tended to trade in an ever-narrower range.
Traders were meanwhile waiting for terms of the Swiss Federal Treasury's bond auction at around 1200 GMT Thursday.

The auction reopens the outstanding 4-1/2 percent June 2007 Federal bond CH470458=. Some traders believed the issue would meet poor demand and they were prepared to short the issue, but others believed it might actually be a success, in which case they saw a chance for a short squeeze in the market.
The Treasury set the maximum market allocation for the bonds at one billion Swiss francs.
